Collectively, the two-tiered framework establishes a paradigm, under which owners and operators of Class VI geologic
sequestration wells must demonstrate the financial means to cover the costs of: (1) well construction; (2) injection, operations &
monitoring (e.g., Area of Review reevaluation & corrective action), (3) injection well plugging, (4) post-injection site care & site
closure, and (5) emergency & remedial response.

An effective financial assurance framework will assure funds are available to pay for activities necessary to detect problems
before they adversely impact public welfare or the environment, and finance remedial action should such action become
necessary. The USEPA’s financial responsibility guidance offers suggested standards for financial responsibility, as well as
recommendations related to the wording of key financial terms, procedures for funding financial instruments, and procedures for
drawing down (or reimbursing costs) from financial instruments.
